name: Ulnar-palmar approach to the distal radius
region: ulnar volar wrist and distal forearm
corridor: Between ulnar neurovascular bundle and flexor tendons, with flexors and median nerve retracted radially

positioning.text: Position supine with the arm on a hand table and forearm supinated for ulnar-volar access.

setup.text: Map ulnar bundle, median nerve, carpal tunnel, lunate facet and sigmoid notch; prepare magnification and vascular control.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark ulna, wrist crease, pisiform, FCU, palmaris longus, flexor-tendon mass, and ulnar pulse.

incision.text: Begin at the wrist crease parallel to the ulna and extend proximally; extend across the crease into palm when carpal-tunnel or radiocarpal access is required.

superficial_interval.text: Identify the ulnar artery and nerve and develop the plane between them and the flexor tendons.

deep_interval.text: Retract flexor tendons and median nerve radially, expose pronator quadratus, and elevate only the ulnar portion required to reach distal radius.

layers.text: Skin, palmar fascia, ulnar bundle-flexor interval, flexor layer with median nerve, pronator quadratus, then volar-ulnar radius.

structures_encountered.text: Ulnar artery and nerve, flexor tendons, median nerve, pronator quadratus, lunate facet, sigmoid notch, capsule, DRUJ, and distal ulna are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Ulnar artery and nerve, median nerve and palmar cutaneous branch, flexor tendons, palmar radiocarpal ligaments, TFCC, and DRUJ cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Keep the ulnar bundle continuously identified and do not confuse an extensile distal continuation with a complete carpal-tunnel release unless decompression is intended.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid sustained radial traction on median nerve and flexors or ulnar pressure on the neurovascular bundle.

exposure.text: Exposes lunate facet, sigmoid notch, palmar capsule, DRUJ, distal ulna, and carpal tunnel when extended.

limitations.text: Provides poor access to the radial styloid and radial column compared with modified Henry or radial-column approaches.

extensions.text: Extend distally for carpal-tunnel and radiocarpal exposure or combine with radial-volar/dorsal approaches for other columns.

indications.text: Use for isolated lunate-facet and volar-ulnar fragments, sigmoid-notch/DRUJ injuries, and selected high-energy fractures requiring extensile ulnar access.

relative_contraindications.text: Use modified Henry for routine radial-column patterns and avoid compromised ulnar-palmar skin or an unmanageable ulnar neurovascular corridor.

implant_implications.text: Supports fragment-specific volar-ulnar fixation; keep hardware clear of flexors, DRUJ, and radiocarpal joint.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use PA, lateral, oblique, tilted lateral, and DRUJ views to verify lunate-facet capture, sigmoid-notch congruity, and screw containment.

closure.text: Repair pronator quadratus when possible, verify flexor glide and ulnar/median nerve function, and close without constricting the bundle.

complications.text: Complications include ulnar or median neuropathy, arterial injury, flexor-tendon irritation, carpal-tunnel symptoms, DRUJ stiffness, joint penetration, and wound problems.

bailouts.text: Add a separate radial or dorsal exposure when other columns remain uncontrolled rather than over-retracting neurovascular structures.

procedure_applications.condition: A lunate-facet, sigmoid-notch, volar-ulnar, DRUJ, or high-energy pattern requires direct ulnar-volar control
The approach is extended distally for indicated median-nerve decompression

questions.question: What is the key interval?
questions.answer: Between the ulnar artery/nerve and the flexor tendons.

questions.question: Which fragments are best exposed?
questions.answer: The lunate facet and sigmoid-notch/volar-ulnar region.
